body:
DELIVERED + codex-verified. Commits 6793e379 + 7f2ece15.
FIXED the single-writer in-commit duplicate-unique-key recovery poison (the bead's bug): a commit_transition
whose entries enqueue two lifecycle items sharing the same UNIQUE typed-index key on the composed sqlite_log
backend previously appended its batch DURABLY then failed apply (relational index_validate_push was a no-op;
uniqueness was enforced only at apply time) -> durable-but-unappliable batch -> recovery poison.
Now SqliteProjectionStore::index_validate_push (relational.rs:10120) + SqliteRelational::index_validate_push
(:9258) reject the colliding entry at VALIDATION (before the durable append) via validate_typed_unique_push
(:1507), which derives the unique typed-index keys IDENTICALLY to the apply-time enforcement (same
typed_index_keys_for_entity + index_is_unique + queue typed_indexes) and checks the full candidate set against
(a) the other items staged in THIS commit AND (b) the durable DB (read-only rolled-back tx). The colliding
entry becomes Rejected(Conflict) (mixed commit, consistent with in-memory); the appended batch is appliable.
Test composed_commit_duplicate_unique_index.rs covers both composed sqlite backends; PRE-FIX poison proven
(reverting the impl to no-op makes it fail with the durable-unappliable batch).

SCOPE (honest): the poison is SQLITE_LOG-specific. postgres relational does NOT support commit_transition
(no supports_commit_transition override -> Unavailable) AND commits append+apply in one transaction (a failed
apply rolls back the append), so it is structurally not poison-vulnerable — the untested postgres change from
the first pass was REVERTED (postgres source is byte-identical to baseline except a scope-note comment).

Codex adversarial review: key-derivation-matches-apply SOUND, no-false-positive SOUND, no-leaked-writes/deadlock
SOUND. One narrow residual codex flagged (NOT this bug, and pre-existing): a CROSS-INSTANCE same-epoch TOCTOU —
two concurrent writers AT THE SAME EPOCH could each validate a key as free before either appends. Codex confirms
this is unreachable "under a strict single-writer-per-epoch assumption," which is exactly the epoch-fencing
ownership invariant (ADR-009/TD-003): a superseded owner is EpochFenced before append; the expected_epoch=None
path assumes actual sole ownership. So it requires violating the single-owner-per-epoch model to trigger; it is a
general property of the log-append-before-apply architecture (a separate concern from this bead's single-writer
in-commit-duplicate bug), documented here, not separately filed.

Verify (independent, LIVE PG reachable): sqlite poison test 2 passed; pqueue-postgres 0-failed (30/32/41/59/3
passed); pqueue-sqlite + pqueue-conformance + pqueue-engine 503 passed, 0 failed; fmt clean; clippy PASS.
summary: sqlite_log in-commit duplicate-unique-key poison fixed (validation matches apply, both composed sqlite backends); postgres structurally not vulnerable (reverted); codex-verified; cross-instance same-epoch TOCTOU gated by ownership documented
